final_recommendation: The room converged on a dual-track rescue: CHF 50 billion SNB liquidity facility live Monday 06:00 with CHF 5 billion pre-positioned buffer, paired with UBS announcing active merger talks at 07:00. Integration triggers at CHF 4.8 billion outflow within four hours. Public exposure capped at CHF 105 billion (CHF 100B solvency + CHF 5B operational buffer). Framework published tonight with explicit creditor hierarchy and liability allocation to secure UBS commitment.
minority_objections: FINMA initially resisted publishing 'absolute limit' language due to legal exposure if cap breached
AT1 representative repeatedly demanded explicit write-down sequence in main statement, not annexes
key_conflicts: Federal Council vs FINMA on whether CHF 100B cap should be labeled 'absolute' or 'current exposure'—resolved by adding resolution-rules clause
UBS CEO vs Federal Council on liability allocation clarity—UBS demanded written guarantees on legacy liabilities staying in wind-down before committing to Monday announcement
Multiple participants vs SNB on settlement friction risk—resolved by ring-fencing CHF 15B for UBS integration and pre-positioning CHF 5B retail buffer
key_concessions: Federal Council raised public exposure from CHF 100B to CHF 105B to accommodate operational buffer
FINMA agreed to publish AT1 hierarchy in main statement (not just annex) to secure creditor confidence
UBS secured written guarantee that losses beyond CHF 100B don't flow to UBS shareholders
SNB committed to CHF 1B pre-positioned cash in CS operational account visible Monday morning
red_lines: UBS: will not announce merger talks without written confirmation that legacy litigation/pension liabilities stay in wind-down entity
Federal Council: CHF 100B (later 105B) is absolute ceiling on taxpayer solvency exposure—losses beyond trigger creditor write-downs
UBS: will not absorb liabilities if CHF 100B cap breach flows to UBS shareholders
SNB: liquidity bridge only—will not commit open-ended exposure without merger backstop
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Legal defensibility of publishing explicit integration trigger (CHF 4.8B) before deal finalized—could create contractual obligations
Operational risk of 90-minute UBS cutover window during active deposit flight
Market reaction if collateral haircuts tighten Monday morning despite locked framework
Litigation risk from AT1 holders if liquidity assistance is later claimed to alter subordination
downstream_risk_variables: Whether CHF 50B liquidity + UBS announcement actually stops deposit flight or merely slows it
Whether 5-minute retail settlement holds under simultaneous CHF 2.5B+ stress volume
Whether publishing CHF 4.8B trigger creates self-fulfilling run to that threshold
Whether UBS board actually approves merger after seeing Monday morning flows
Whether AT1 holders litigate despite published hierarchy language
uncertainty_notes: The room locked a detailed operational framework but left unresolved: (1) whether UBS board will actually approve merger if Monday flows stabilize below CHF 4.8B threshold—no binding commitment, only conditional announcement; (2) whether published trigger creates self-fulfilling panic as depositors race to withdraw before CHF 4.8B hit; (3) legal enforceability of liability allocation if actual losses exceed projections; (4) whether 90-minute cutover window creates visible system handoff that triggers secondary flight.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: SNB repeatedly stated CHF 50B liquidity 'buys us the week' but is 'a bridge, not solvency cover'—drove the parallel UBS merger track as necessary backstop, not optional Plan B
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: UBS merger became the binding solution—UBS CEO's Monday 07:00 announcement commitment and CHF 4.8B integration trigger were written into the framework as operational constraints
marker_evidence.government_support: CHF 100B (later 105B) public backstop was the prerequisite for UBS participation—Federal Council signature on loss protection was UBS's non-negotiable condition for Monday announcement
marker_evidence.client_flight: CHF 5B/hour threshold, CHF 4.8B integration trigger, and entire settlement architecture (5-minute retail clears, ring-fenced queues) were designed around stopping deposit flight—it drove every operational decision
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: AT1 write-down sequence was extensively discussed and codified in published hierarchy, but it did not change the rescue structure—it was accommodated within the existing framework, not a binding constraint on the deal
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: Common equity vs AT1 sequencing was debated and resolved by publishing explicit hierarchy, but the resolution did not alter the CHF 100B cap, UBS terms, or integration mechanics—acknowledged and documented, not decisive
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: AT1 representative warned of litigation risk if hierarchy unclear, and FINMA added language to mitigate it—but this was defensive documentation, not a factor that changed the rescue structure or numbers
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: 22:00 publication deadline and 06:00 Monday liquidity window drove every drafting decision—FINMA's refusal to delay for further legal review, Federal Council's insistence on publishing trigger numbers tonight, all constrained by Monday open
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: The entire framework (CHF 50B live at 06:00, UBS statement at 07:00, published triggers) was architected to prevent Monday panic—the fear of market open without credible plan drove the timeline and public commitments
